_comment: The contexts branch protection requires on main, committed so
scripts/check_required_check_substance.py can grade them.
GITHUB_TOKEN cannot be granted administration:read, so the API copy is
unreadable from CI and this file is the only list available there. The gate
compares the two whenever a token that CAN read protection is present, and
says plainly when it could not.
enforced_from is the floor for grading. Runs before it are counted and
printed but not failed: they are the measured pre-fix history, and failing
them forever would teach everyone to ignore this check. Over the 100 most
recent successful push runs on main before this landed, 'docker compose up
- full stack' booted nothing on 27 of them and 'Backup - destroy - restore'
rehearsed nothing on 74. Moving this date forward to silence a finding is
the one edit that makes the gate worthless; it is also the only edit that
can, which is why it lives in a reviewed file rather than a flag.
It is set just after the commit that made every required check grade every
commit that lands, because runs before that point were correct about a tree
that had not yet been fixed. A window holding no runs is tolerated for
seven days and then fails, so parking this date in the future cannot
silence the gate for long.
The Security workflow's scanner jobs were hard gates that blocked nothing:
Trivy fails outright on a fixable HIGH/CRITICAL and had been red on main for
nine consecutive runs with nothing to stop a merge, because only
security-audit was required. Four of the six are promoted here. All six
were checked for the defect that makes a required check worthless rather
than assumed safe: security.yml declares no paths filter and no job-level
if:, and across 40 pull_request runs every one of the six reported a real
conclusion and none reported skipped - GitHub counts a skipped check as
passing, so requiring one that skips on pull requests would recreate the
defect this repository has now fixed twice.
'Semgrep (ratcheted)' and 'IaC scan (checkov, ratcheted)' each used to
carry a continue-on-error step whose outcome no later step read, so the
job could report success over a step that failed and the Actions API
cannot see it. Both are now closed the way the gate's own message
prescribes: the scan step carries an id and a blocking step reads
steps.<id>.outcome == 'failure'. That step sits AHEAD of the ratchet,
because a scan that dies part-way still writes a short report and the
ratchet's shrink-only arm would answer it by asking for the ceiling to be
lowered - baking the broken scan in. checkov additionally had its pip
install moved out of the absorbed step into a blocking one, and its
trailing '|| true' replaced by an explicit exit-code rule: 0 and 1 are a
scan that ran, anything above is a scan that did not.
'IaC scan (checkov, ratcheted)' is promoted here on the strength of that
fix.
'Semgrep (ratcheted)' is deliberately STILL NOT required, and that is a
decision rather than an oversight. Do not add it here without reading
this paragraph: closing its absorbed-failure hole and requiring it are
separate questions, and only the first was answered yes. It is
non-deterministic on an unchanged tree - four pull requests on one base,
changing nothing but a lockfile, run within thirteen minutes, split
102/40 and 101/39 over the identical 387 rules and 2267 files, with the
obvious mechanisms eliminated and the whole measurement recorded in
.security/allowlist.yml. Requiring it would red roughly one pull request
in twenty for a reason no author can act on, and the only remedy is a
re-run - which teaches people to re-run until green rather than to read
the finding, and that is how a required check stops meaning anything.
'Previous minor to this tree, with data present' is promoted here, and
the workflow had to change shape first. People upgrade, and until now a
pull request could break the upgrade path with both upgrade tests red or
never run: neither upgrade-test.yml nor integration.yml's upgrade leg was
required. Promoting it as it stood would have been worse than leaving it,
because upgrade-test.yml was path-filtered on both triggers and a
workflow that does not trigger creates no check run at all - the quiet
failure, not a red one. Measured over the 18 most recently merged pull
requests, reading every page of commits/{sha}/check-runs (113-143 checks
each, so the one-page cap was not the cause): the context was absent from
18 of 18, and none of the 18 had touched a filtered path. Requiring that
shape would have deadlocked the queue on the first pull request after it.
The filter is gone rather than moved into the jobs. integration.yml needs
the job-level form because a disaster-recovery rehearsal costs 15
minutes; this one is 1-3 minutes measured over its own runs, so it now
carries no filter anywhere and no job-level or step-level if: at all. It
cannot rehearse nothing the way 'Backup - destroy - restore' did on 74 of
100 runs, and that is a property a reader can check by looking rather
than a behaviour someone has to go and measure.
The cross-major legs added alongside it are deliberately NOT required.
A matrix job's context name contains the matrix value, so adding or
renaming a starting version would orphan a required context that can then
never report - the same defect in a new costume.
'Cross-store isolation (Neo4j + Redis + ClickHouse + Kafka)' is promoted here
on measured history, and the workflow had to change shape twice first.
History: over 82 push runs to main since 2026-07-12 it failed three times -
one real regression, the workflow's own first run, and one where the runner
never attached (steps: [] over 66 minutes against a 20-minute budget).
Across its last 100 runs of all events: 80 success, 4 failure (all four the
same regression), 16 cancelled by the concurrency group, zero container
flakes. Job execution over the 40 most recent successes: min 46s, median
Shape, first change: it was path-filtered on both triggers, so it created
no check run at all on a pull request that missed the filter - and that is
how the regression merged ungraded, its head graded by the offline
isolation job instead. Requiring it in that shape would have deadlocked
the queue on the first pull request that touched nothing it names. The
filter is gone rather than moved into the job, for the reason recorded
above against 'Previous minor to this tree, with data present': a
job-level if: produces a check run whose conclusion is skipped, GitHub
counts a skipped check as passing, and the pull request would merge having
never run the assertion. At a 52-second median the job is cheaper than
that one, so it now carries no filter anywhere and no if: on any assertive
step.
Shape, second change: two of its three steps could still skip, which is
the 'Backup - destroy - restore' defect exactly. Measured with the job's
own dependency set and no containers running, all three steps reported
success: test_live_stores 4 skipped of 4, test_retro_hunt_live 17 skipped
of 19, test_backtest_lake_live 12 skipped of 15 - a green tick on the
four stores in the check's own title having connected to none of them.
LIVE_STORES_REQUIRED and RETRO_HUNT_LAKE_LIVE_REQUIRED now join
BACKTEST_LAKE_LIVE_REQUIRED, so an unset address, an uninstalled client or
an unreachable warehouse fails. Verified both ways against real
containers: 38 assertions pass with the stores up, and all three steps
fail with them down.
